metaData.originalTitle: 我把自己的 IP 配图技能开源了 顺手做了 31 个现成角色
metaData.title: I Open-Sourced My IP Illustration Skill and Built 31 Ready-to-Use Characters
metaData.oneSentenceSummary: The author open-sources their daily AI illustration workflow "Xiao Hu IP Studio," featuring 31 original characters, multiple art style skins, and a systematic illustration methodology that enables AI to read articles, plan visuals, and generate consistent illustrations automatically.
metaData.summary: The article details the author's open-source project "Xiao Hu IP Studio" — an Agent Skill-based AI illustration tool. Key highlights include: 31 original characters in a unified hand-drawn style (15 workplace personas + 16 pun-based memes), allowing users to start immediately without building their own IP; multiple art style skins (blind box figurines, black-and-white line art, flat vector, watercolor, etc.) that adapt to article tone while preserving character recognizability; and a solidified illustration decision workflow — paragraph-by-paragraph review, categorized illustration, and self-check rework — ensuring every image precisely serves its content. The author also shares the "Three IP Laws" and "Four Hard Rules" of character design, along with foolproof installation instructions (one sentence lets AI install itself), supporting tools like Claude Code and Codex. The article concludes with acknowledgments to inspiring predecessor projects (Xiao Hei, Baoyu, etc.) and is released under the MIT license.

mainPoints.point: Open-sources a standardized AI illustration skill where the core is workflow rather than single-image generation capability.
mainPoints.explanation: The tool provides a complete pipeline from reading articles → selecting paragraphs → categorizing → conceptualizing → checking, offering far more control than standalone image generation and ensuring illustration quality and consistency.

mainPoints.point: 31 ready-made original characters lower the barrier to entry, with support for changing skins without changing characters.
mainPoints.explanation: Users can pick characters to use directly or substitute their own IP; multiple art style skins can switch according to article tone while core features remain unchanged, maintaining recognizability.

mainPoints.point: Proposes three IP laws: 'weak persona / contrast > strong styling,' 'characters are emotional synonyms,' and 'distinctiveness lies in posture and attitude.'
mainPoints.explanation: Based on the author's experience, these character design principles emphasize shaping IP through minimal forms and emotional resonance rather than piling on stylistic details.

mainPoints.point: The illustration decision workflow is solidified into four hard rules to prevent AI from cutting corners or going off track.
mainPoints.explanation: Paragraph-by-paragraph review (no skipping), categorized illustration (emotion/explanation/comic), categorize before drawing, and post-drawing self-check — these rules improve the match between illustrations and content.

keyQuotes: A pretty picture that gets the point wrong is worse than an ugly one.
Without it, this image wouldn't work.
Weak persona / contrast > strong styling — the more you rely on stylistic spectacle to stand out, the more you fail.
A character is an 'emotional synonym' — it makes people see it and say 'that's me.'

relatedArticles.title: Harness Is Not the Goal, Knowledge Is the Moat — Knowledge Accumulation Practices of an AI Engineering Delivery Team
relatedArticles.oneSentenceSummary: Based on the engineering delivery practices of an AI Team, this article proposes that knowledge accumulation is more important than workflow orchestration, and systematically introduces a complete methodology encompassing a five-layer knowledge storage architecture, a three-level maturity system, and how workflows serve knowledge accumulation.

relatedArticles.title: Redefining Skill Development: A Step-by-Step Guide & One-Stop Development Assistant Launch
relatedArticles.oneSentenceSummary: This article systematically introduces the concept of AI Agent Skill, including its directory structure, writing standards, release process, and cross-platform challenges. It also launches a one-stop Skill development assistant, skill-dev-aio, designed to free developers from tedious tool learning and allow them to focus on experience and judgment.

relatedArticles.title: Understanding Hermes in One Article: How the New Top-Tier Agent Self-Evolves from Experience
relatedArticles.oneSentenceSummary: This article provides an in-depth analysis of the core innovation of the Hermes Agent—the Skills closed-loop system—detailing its complete implementation mechanism, from experience extraction and knowledge storage to intelligent retrieval and self-improvement, along with its engineering trade-offs and security considerations.

relatedArticles.title: AI R&D Automation: Wiki Knowledge Base + Skill Pack
relatedArticles.oneSentenceSummary: This article details how to build a continuously growing team knowledge base and a supporting expert skill pack based on the LLM-Wiki model and the Obsidian platform to achieve AI-driven R&D automation.

relatedArticles.title: OpenClaw and Hermes: A Comprehensive Review of AI Agent Architecture from Source Code
relatedArticles.oneSentenceSummary: This article systematically summarizes the design trade-offs and engineering practices of Agent architecture in core modules such as message routing, memory management, context engineering, and security sandboxing, through an in-depth analysis of the source code of two open-source AI Agent frameworks: OpenClaw and Hermes.

relatedArticles.title: Understanding Harness Engineering: Finding the Shell That Keeps AI from Going Rogue—Insights from 14 Engineering Articles | Hao's Trend Talk
relatedArticles.oneSentenceSummary: This article provides an in-depth analysis of "Harness Engineering," a core technology in the AI Agent field. It reveals how to compensate for model shortcomings through a three-layer management architecture and proposes the logic of "Compensation Surface Migration" that evolves with model capabilities.

relatedArticles.title: Investing 10,000 RMB in AI: A Year of Tools, Practices, and Reflections
relatedArticles.oneSentenceSummary: A systematic summary of a veteran developer's practical experience in the AI wave, covering everything from MAC toolchain optimization and Harness Engineering architectural constraints to building an Agent-driven automated learning loop.

relatedArticles.title: One Image to Generate a Real-Time Conversational Video Character: Runway Brings Video Generation to the Dialogue Scene
relatedArticles.oneSentenceSummary: Runway Characters generates real-time conversational video characters from a single reference image, pushing AI video from offline generation to real-time interaction, with agent capabilities such as visual understanding, knowledge base, and tool calling.

relatedArticles.title: AI Learns to Video Call You, Just Like a Real Person
relatedArticles.oneSentenceSummary: Alibaba Tongyi Lab's Wan Team released Wan Streamer, an end-to-end Transformer model that achieves sub-second full-duplex real-time audio-video conversation, synchronously generating speech and facial video.

relatedArticles.title: Most Companies Have Data but No Memory. No Matter How Many AI Agents You Add, They Won't Work
relatedArticles.oneSentenceSummary: This article delves into Ashwin Gopinath's concept of the 'Company Brain,' arguing that the real barrier to enterprise AI adoption is not insufficient model capability, but the lack of organizational memory—the executable chain of judgment derived from scattered data.
